newsitem.title: USA: First Charter issued regulatory directive.
newsitem.headline: First Charter issued regulatory directive.

text.p: First Charter Bank NA said Friday the Comptroller of the Currency issued a directive to the bank setting capital ratio requirements and calling for measures pertaining to its lending practices.
In addition, First Charter said it agreed in principle to sell $5.0 million of convertible preferred stock to investors, boosting its capital by $4.6 million.
The deal is subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close by Sept. 30, or as soon thereafter as possible.

The comptroller's directive requires that by Sept. 30, or by complying with a plan approved by the comptroller, the bank must achieve and maintain Tier 1 capital at least equal to 11 percent of risk weighted assets and Tier 1 capital at least equal to five percent of actual adjusted assets.
Within 45 days, or in an approved plan, the board must appoint a senior lending officer who can ensure the safe and sound operation of the bank's lending function.
Within 30 days, the bank must formulate and implement an effective independent loan and lease review program to identify problem loans and leases in the bank's portfolio.
